answer: The falcon detector writes to summit, and spiral publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, and therefore the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 209 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 57 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 24 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
